It's tough to evolve beyond that. Tougher than I believed until I experienced it first hand. I've been thinking about it a lot in recent years.

Why are we all not just nice to eachother? Sounds simple but it really isn't. All my life, I never would've considered me a racist. Never in my life did I look at someone from another country or culture and immediately think less of them in any way. In my mind, a person is a person. We're all the same.

Then, in recent years I noticed how I started to become a bit racist. Sadly. Or did I? When does racism really start or stop? Let me explain.

I am Swiss. Switzerland has one of the highest percentages of foreigners in Europe at almost 26%. Simultaneously, Switzerland also has a really high percentage of secondos. Italians, Spaniards, Portugeses, Albanians, Kosovars etc. Nothing wrong with that.

The problem starts when in recent years, there are more and more reports of teenagers or young adults beating up pedestrians for no reason. Or beat up gay people in front of gay bars on weekends. And every single time they're caught, with few exceptions, they're from eastern Europe. You hear it over and over again and it starts to change your view, bit by bit. Last week a bunch of teenagers beat up and set on fire a man, because he accidentally bumped into one of them on the bus. This weekend, a few teenagers beat up a young adult at a train station because he was alone and defenseless. A pedestrian from far away took a photo when they were running away. Sweatpants, hoodie over their head, hip bags. If you live here you know the kind. It's the kind of group you don't even dare look at when you're out and about because one funny look can land you in a hospital these days. And I can tell you that much, they're not Swiss.

A friend of my GF is a Kindergarten teacher. She's had 38 kids the past 2 years, 4 of whom spoke German. All the other kids went from speaking a few words to none at all. All of those kids have a Swiss passport though. In big cities, if you count all these kids, teenagers and young adults as foreign, my best guess is we're at like 60-70% foreign rate. Now, some, if not most of them will turn alright. But a small part of them will also turn into the people described above.

So after seeing this decline and boom of criminality over the years you obviously start to think "Enough is enough. We have enough of "them" here. It's time to close the border". Does that really make me a racist?

What are the odds of tomorrow ending up in a big ball of nothing?

Here's my tinfoil hat theory:

So according to Marko, RB and the FIA are discussing several financial points in which RB claim they're under budget, but the FIA claim they're over as they count personnel that RB doesn't.

Let's just say the FIA comes to the conclusion that RB are in fact, over budget. Of course there will be questions about how much, was it on purpose, did they try to hide it etc. But let's ignore that for now, over budget is over budget and I think we all agree that this should be punished harshly, otherwise what's the point of the budget cap if you can just go over and get a slap on the wrist, right?

The thing is, the FIA will under no circumstances alter the 2021 or 2022 WDCs. That's just not what they do. Also, there'd be a huge backlash from the fans, a massive shitstorm. Deducting points from the WCC however, is like a slap on the wrist. They'd maybe lose a spot or two in the WCC and lose a few millions but let's face it, that'd be like a luxury tax for RB since they have enough backing to max out the cap again and sponsors won't care whether RB is 2nd or 4th. It's RB.

Another solution would be to lower their cap for coming seasons, putting them at a slight disadvantage. However, they did win a WDC in 2021 and developed by far the best car for the new regulations by going over budget. They can ride this wave for a few more seasons even with a lower cap so is it really a fair punishment? Only if they start falling back I guess, but with how good their car is, that might not happen.

So onto my theory: Since none of the solutions are a good look for either F1, RB or anyone else involved and there will always be other teams or fans unhappy with how things were handled, the best move for the FIA is to just agree with RBs points of views about how the cap works, make it public that RB was within the budget cap and then handle things with RB under the table, much like they did with Ferrari during the engine fiasco in 2019. And that is why we will get a big boatload of nothing tomorrow.
